channel.title: The h5i Blog
channel.description: Engineering essays on verifiable Rust web applications, Lean 4 proofs, web security testing, and agent isolation.

item.title: Building a Verifiable Web Framework in Rust
item.description: Why h5i-app puts a small Rust decision kernel between Axum handlers and storage, then translates that kernel to Lean 4 for proofs.

item.title: I Tried to Verify Popular Rust OSS with Lean 4, but Found Bugs Instead
item.description: Failed proof attempts led to confirmed Rust OSS bugs: an unscoped delete, a playlist metadata leak, and unbounded policy expansion.

item.title: AI-Powered Web Security Testing: h5i vs. Burp, ZAP, and Caido
item.description: Compare Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, Caido, and h5i by the investigation each supports: manual proxy work, scanning, agent tooling, and browser-to-HTTP testing.

item.title: Sandboxing AI Agents: Isolation, Security, and Prompt Injection
item.description: Why an agent sandbox must include child processes and browsers, how isolation tiers differ, and what prompt injection can still reach.

item.title: Auditing AI Agent Workflows with Execution Evidence
item.description: A patch shows what changed, but reviewing agent work also needs commands, browser activity, network decisions, missing evidence, and a controlled export.
